title: Tally: a form builder that works like a doc

source.text: Tally: a form builder that works like a doc, free with a paid Pro plan, launch country BE (Belgium, selling worldwide online). Score it as of 2020-06-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: two bootstrapped developers. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug tally-forms.

problem: Building a good-looking online form takes a drag-and-drop builder, and the polished ones (Typeform) charge for basics like responses and logic.
customer: Makers, indie founders, no-code builders and small teams who need forms (waitlists, surveys, applications) and already work in doc-style tools like Notion
solution: A web form builder you type into like a document (no drag-and-drop), with a generous free plan and a paid Pro plan for advanced features
claims: a form builder that works like a doc
free with a paid Pro plan

context.edge: two developers who can build the product themselves

assumptions: Pro price assumed at $29/month (USD, worldwide), in the range of Typeform's ~$40 average price (2018)
Bootstrapped: budget near zero beyond hosting and tools; founders' own time unpaid at first
Goal assumed to be a bootstrapped startup replacing two salaries
Main channel assumed organic: Product Hunt, maker communities and a 'Made with Tally' badge on free forms
Scored as of 2020-06-01 with evidence published on or before that date
